subject: Architecture
title: Bosco Verticale: A Forest on a Tower
description: Learn Bosco Verticale: A Forest on a Tower in one minute.

hook.text: Two residential towers in Milan hold 900 trees, 5,000 shrubs, and 11,000 plants on their balconies.

buildup.text: Bosco Verticale — 'Vertical Forest' — was designed by Stefano Boeri to bring nature into dense city life.

discovery.text: The plants filter dust, produce oxygen, and shade apartments — reducing air conditioning needs by 30%.

twist.text: Maintaining the trees requires 'flying gardeners' who rappel down the facade on ropes to prune branches.

climax.text: The concept is spreading — vertical forests are now planned in Nanjing, Utrecht, Cairo, and São Paulo.

punchline.text: They planted a forest on a skyscraper. Now cities want their own.

quiz.question: How are trees maintained on Bosco Verticale's balconies?
options: Gardeners rappel down the facade on ropes
Residents maintain their own trees with provided kits
